Insurance companies "negotiate" (more like strongarm) prices for individual services from individual providers, and each company sets its own prices, and what it will and won't pay for.

So, in this case, Tricare would have said "No, we're not paying for that under these circumstances." Meanwhile, a private insurance company would have already agreed to pay for the service as laid out in the consumer policy agreement.

Most providers will not order a service that they know won't be paid for by insurance. Because when a service is ordered, like an MRI, two phone calls go out: one to the radiological provider, and one to the insurance company. If they know beforehand the insurance is going to tell them to take a hike, they are putting another provider at risk of incurring bad debt, and losing significant amount of money.

So then, instead of refusing to pay the provider, they simply refuse to reimburse the patient.
